A 3-month history of activity-exacerbated pain localized to the right thumb base and radial wrist, radiating proximally to the elbow. Pain is provoked by weight-bearing grip (e.g., holding an infant), consistent with mechanical stress on the first dorsal extensor compartment.

- Provisional diagnosis explicitly endorsed as de Quervain tenosynovitis based on symptom pattern and Finkelstein’s test  

[GAPS]  
- Formal assessment of thumb opposition strength and range of motion (to better exclude basal joint OA or CMC instability)  
- Ultrasound findings of first dorsal compartment (tendon sheath thickening, fluid, hyperemia) — definitive confirmatory test  
- Radiographs of thumb/wrist — to assess for radial styloid spur, CMC joint space narrowing, or other bony contributors  
- Phalen’s test and Tinel’s sign results — though negative sensory symptoms make CTS unlikely, formal testing would strengthen exclusion  
- CRP/ESR — to objectively assess for subclinical inflammation if diagnosis remains uncertain  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
De Quervain tenosynovitis
